context.body: Genesis through Deuteronomy distinguishes requests, responses, priestly formulas, intercession, restitution, pardon, retained consequence, and stated refusal to pardon. The bounded source is Leviticus 6:1–7.
context.label: Narrative or literary frame

observations.body: Deception, robbery, lost property, restitution with an added fifth, a guilt offering, atonement.
observations.label: Restitution precedes offering and forgiveness: action

payload.posture: Read Leviticus 6:1–7 as requests, law, and pardon evidence before carrying it into another source.
payload.tension: The passage gives bounded Forgiveness evidence, but it does not make this request, response, condition, means, or outcome a universal procedure: Deception, robbery, lost property, restitution with an added fifth, a guilt offering, atonement, and forgiveness appear in one procedure.
payload.title: Restitution precedes offering and forgiveness
